title: Evaluator CLI and Sidecar Plugin Spec (v0)
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary

This spec describes the Evaluator CLI (evalctl) and the Sidecar Plugin Contract for Redwood's eval harness. It covers command semantics, manifest fields, telemetry, failure handling and rollout for hosted and private (dedicated/VPC) evaluator deployments, so teams and tenants can plug in evaluators consistently and auditably, including during quant shadowing.

Goals
- One stable CLI for local, CI and on-host evaluation runs.
- A minimal sidecar plugin API so third-party or customer evaluators can join the shadow mesh.
- Required telemetry and artifacts for traceability, reproducibility and automated triage.
- Clear failure semantics plus a safe stop/rollback path for risky sweeps.

Scope and non-goals
- Scope: token-level and prompt-level evaluators, synthetic probe runners, function-call validators, compact shadow probes.
- Non-goals: Console/UI integration and dataset catalog formats (see prompt-sets-and-benchmarks).

Terminology
- evalctl: evaluator CLI used by CI, local dev and on-host runners.
- sidecar plugin: executable or HTTP service implementing the plugin contract.
- probe: a single test input used by an evaluator.

Contract overview
- Protocols: stdin/stdout JSON lines and HTTP/JSON REST (v1).
- Manifests: every plugin ships a YAML manifest listing capabilities, resource hints and artifact outputs.
- Outputs: a standardized results envelope and an artifacts index.

Evaluator CLI (evalctl)
1. evalctl init --manifest <path>: validates the manifest and runs a dry-run capability test. Exit codes: 0=ok, 2=validation error, 3=permission/fatal.
2. evalctl run --manifest <path> --workdir <dir> [--slice <slice-id>] [--mode local|ci|shadow] [--concurrency N] [--telemetry-level minimal|standard|verbose]
3. evalctl collect --workdir <dir> --artifact-index out/index.json --output <s3://...|gs://...|local>
4. evalctl stop --run-id <id> --graceful/--force

Example usage:
  $ evalctl run --manifest ./plugin.yaml --workdir /tmp/eval-087 --mode shadow --concurrency 4
  $ evalctl collect --workdir /tmp/eval-087 --artifact-index out/index.json --output s3://eval-artifacts/tenant-a/2026-01-15

Plugin manifest (YAML) - minimal example
---
name: functional-reranker-evaluator
version: 0.2.4
protocols: ["stdin-jsonl", "http-json-v1"]
capabilities:
  - functioncall-validation
  - multiseed
resource_hints:
  cpu: "2"
  mem_mb: "4096"
  gpu: "0"
outputs:
  results_envelope: "results.jsonl"
  artifacts_index: "index.json"
telemetry_endpoint: "https://telemetry.redwood.internal/ingest"
health_check: "/healthz"
---

Fields explained
- name, version: semver for promotion gating; a new minor version needs review and a rollout plan.
- protocols: supported IPC forms (at least one).
- capabilities: routing tags for the eval mesh (functioncall-validation, kv-cache-sensitive, quant-aware).
- resource_hints: best-effort orchestrator hints.
- outputs: workdir-relative paths the plugin must write.

Sidecar plugin API (HTTP JSON v1)
  GET /healthz -> 200 {"status":"ok","version":"0.2.4"}
  POST /run -> 202 accepts a RunSpec, returns {"run_id":"uuid-v4","eta_seconds": int}
  POST /stop -> 200 accepts {"run_id": ..., "signal": "graceful|force"}
  GET /status?run_id=<id> -> 200 {"run_id":..., "state":"running|completed|failed|stopped","progress":0.0}
  GET /artifact-index?run_id=<id> -> 200 artifacts index JSON

RunSpec JSON (example)
{
  "run_id": "string (optional, auto-generated)",
  "slice_id": "string",
  "probe_manifest": "s3://.../slice-manifest.json",
  "seeds": [42, 7, 1337],
  "mode": "shadow|ci|local",
  "telemetry_level": "minimal|standard|verbose",
  "max_examples": 10000
}

Outputs and artifact index
- Written to workdir/out/<run_id>/: results.jsonl, index.json, optional html-report.zip and debug-traces.tar.gz.

Artifact index JSON (index.json) - required fields
{
  "run_id": "uuid",
  "started_at": "ISO8601",
  "completed_at": "ISO8601",
  "results_file": "results.jsonl",
  "summary": "out/summary.json",
  "checksums": {"results.jsonl":"sha256:..."}
}

ResultEnvelope (one per line in results.jsonl)
- Fields: probe_id, input_hash, output_text, score (optional), metadata (map).
{"probe_id":"anchor-003","input_hash":"sha256:...","output_text":"...","score":0.87,"metadata":{"seed":42,"latency_ms":123}}

Telemetry and observability
- Events: eval.run.start (run_id, plugin_name, slice_id, mode); eval.run.progress (run_id, percent, sampled_latency_ms); eval.run.complete (run_id, result_counts, summary_metrics).
- Stable identifiers: run_id, plugin_name, tenant_id (where applicable), slice_id.
- 1-minute metrics: examples_processed, avg_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, failures_count.

Failure modes and remediation
- Validation errors (exit code 2): invalid manifest or probe format; fail fast in CI and do not promote.
- Runtime OOMs: plugin writes out/error_tombstone.json with reason and recent stderr; orchestrator marks the run failed and triggers host-side capture.
- Silent drift (zero-length results): P1 for shadow runs; automated triage pages eval-oncall when the results rate < 1% of expected for five minutes.

Security and privacy constraints
- Sidecars on private deployments send no telemetry to hosted endpoints unless configured in the manifest and approved by the privacy team.
- Artifacts containing PII are encrypted at rest.

SLOs and gating for promotion
- Correctness SLO for promoted validators: >= 99.0% successful runs on representative slices during a 48-hour shadow window.
- Performance SLO: median per-probe latency within 2x of the canonical evaluator for the same slice.
- Safety gate: >0.5% hallucination-class failures on audited probes blocks auto-promotion.

Onboarding checklist
1. Write the plugin manifest and commit it to the eval repo.
2. Run `evalctl init` locally and clear validation warnings.
3. Run `evalctl run --mode local` on a representative slice and collect artifacts.
4. File a promotion request with telemetry links and artifacts.
5. Complete a 48-hour shadow run with `telemetry_level=standard` and attach the artifact index.
6. Product/ML reviewer and security reviewer sign-off.

Rollout and rollback procedure
- Canary rollout: 0.5% traffic -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%, at least 1 hour steady-state per step for high-cost/nightly jobs.
- Rollback: `evalctl stop --run-id <id> --force` for active runs; remove the manifest from routing and revert the promotion tag.

Operational runbook (fast path)
1. "eval.run.rate-drop" pages eval-oncall.
2. `evalctl status` for the most recent run_ids.
3. `evalctl collect --workdir /srv/eval/<run_id> --output /tmp/collect`; inspect out/error_tombstone.json.
4. For recently promoted manifests, mark them suspect in the promotion registry and roll back.

Ownership and contacts
- Spec owner: Ava Martinez (Applied ML Infra).
- Runtime integration: Runtime Serving team (eng-serving-runtime).
- Observability contract: Eng Platform (dashboards-and-alerts).

Appendix A: Example CI job snippet
```yaml
jobs:
  eval-run:
    steps:
      - checkout
      - run: evalctl init --manifest plugin.yaml
      - run: evalctl run --manifest plugin.yaml --workdir ./work --mode ci --concurrency 2
      - run: evalctl collect --workdir ./work --artifact-index ./work/out/index.json --output s3://eval-ci-artifacts/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}
```

Document history
- 2025-10-06: Created (Ava Martinez).
- 2025-12-02: Added promotion SLOs (Daniel Cho).
- 2026-01-22: Added rollout and rollback procedure.

New evaluator authors should start from the manifest example and `evalctl init`. Policy exceptions (outbound telemetry from private deployments) go to security@redwood.internal via the promotion ticket.
